scenario: A colleague asks to borrow a car for a weekend trip, handing over the key and asking if the borrower can be trusted to protect the vehicle.
A new intern is given access to sensitive client data and asked to input it into the company database without immediate supervision.
A friend suggests splitting the cost of a group dinner by having the host keep the remaining cash from the restaurant bill.
A neighbor leaves their spare house key with a new acquaintance, asking them to water the plants while they are on vacation.
A business partner proposes a joint venture where one party provides the initial capital and the other handles operations, with profit sharing agreed upon but not yet legally binding.
A child is left at a drop-off center for a few hours in an unfamiliar neighborhood while the parent runs an errand.
An online seller sends a package to a buyer who has explicitly stated they cannot verify the goods before payment is processed on a peer-to-peer platform.
A software developer shares their SSH private key with a junior colleague to access a production server for an urgent bug fix.
A host serves homemade wine to guests at a dinner party without explaining the ingredients or the safety of the fermentation process.
A patient allows a new doctor to examine their medical history and physical body, relying on the professional to diagnose a chronic condition.
A friend offers to drive a passenger to an airport early in the morning, with no backup plan if the driver is late.
A company allows an executive to access the financial audit files before the official board meeting, relying on their commitment to confidentiality.
A tenant is allowed to install new fixtures in their rented apartment without the landlord’s immediate oversight, owing them a signed agreement.
A stranger on a hiking trail offers advice on a shortcut that bypasses a known dangerous section of the path.
A bank allows a client to overdraft their checking account during a system error, relying on the client to repay from savings.
A teacher assigns a project to a student, allowing them to submit it late due to a reported family emergency without immediate verification.
A coworker leaves their laptop unlocked and open on their desk while stepping out for coffee, containing unencrypted company projects.
A parent allows a teenager to stay home alone for the first time, giving them access to the home oven and sharp knives.
A ride-share driver accepts a fare from a new user, waiting at the curb based solely on the app’s location data.
A small business owner relies on a freelancer to manage their social media accounts, granting admin access without a written contract.
A friend invites another to co-sign a car loan, sharing financial liability for the asset.
A hospital nurse administers medication to a patient based on a handwritten note from a senior doctor in a different department.
A traveler leaves their passport and room key in the lobby concierge tray to be held while they go out to dinner.
A tech startup founder shares their company’s roadmap with a potential investor before a non-disclosure agreement is signed.
A colleague gives access to their personal phone number for work-related emergencies, trusting it will not be shared with other departments.
A dog owner leaves their pet in the care of a first-time sitter, trusting them to follow feeding instructions.
A government official receives unverified intelligence about a security threat and must decide whether to act on it without further confirmation.
A customer leaves valuable jewelry with a repair shop for cleaning, receiving only a receipt with a serial number.
A friend accepts an invitation to a house party without meeting the host before, relying on the text description of the event.
A company allows its employees to work remotely, trusting they will complete their tasks without physical supervision.
A parent allows a child to buy items from a vending machine with coins, trusting the child to return the correct change.
A doctor prescribes a strong painkiller, trusting the patient will use it only as directed and not share it with others.
A bank tells a customer that their daily transfer limit has been increased pending a manual review, allowing larger transactions.
A friend lends a car to someone who has just passed their driving test, trusting their new skill level.
A school allows students to use the library computers for research without proctoring, trusting they will not access inappropriate content.
A neighbor invites a new family to their house for tea, trusting they will treat the home with respect.
A company relies on its IT department to patch security vulnerabilities within a specific timeframe without immediate verification.
A patient signs a consent form for a experimental treatment, trusting the medical team to disclose all risks.
A hotel guest leaves their luggage in the cloakroom, trusting it will be returned as is the next day.
A friend allows another to use their gym membership, trusting they will not share the locker room code with outsiders.
A business allows a new vendor to invoice before delivery, trusting the quality of the promised goods.
A parent allows a teenager to drive a family member’s car, trusting their ability to park in the driveway.
A library allows patrons to borrow books with a security deposit only, trusting they will not damage the spines.
A friend offers to watch a house, trusting the owner to not leave valuable items visible from the street.
A company relies on its employees to report safety incidents promptly, trusting they are not afraid of retribution.
A patient trusts their physiotherapist’s assessment of their pain levels over their own verbal description.
A traveler relies on a local guide’s knowledge of a hidden restaurant, trusting the food will be safe to eat.
A teacher trusts students’ completed homework, which was not checked for plagiarism before grading.
A friend lends a tool for a weekend DIY project, trusting it will be returned clean and functional.
A company allows its sales team to promise delivery dates to clients, trusting the logistics team to meet them.
